scope: Baseline retained quick-check response criteria (28) and earlier worked examples (7). Earlier examples were visible with their keys; these are recomputations, not a claim of blind solving. New guided/tricky pack not yet seen.

quick_checks: Choose purpose/audience and organise ideas before drafting.
Story: linked events/problem/resolution; information: organised related facts; persuasion: opinion/request and fitting reasons.
Two complete clauses joined with a coordinator; both can stand alone.
Make ideas/meaning and order clear, then edit sentences/conventions.
AC9E2LY06.earlier: Character, setting, problem, events and ending provide linked story notes.

quick_checks: Rehearse to notice clarity/order/delivery, hear feedback and make a purposeful change.
Name the topic and purpose so the audience knows what to expect.
A manageable pace and pauses help listeners process important points.
A visual is useful when it explains the topic/sequence or reminds the speaker rather than merely decorating.
AC9E2LY07.earlier: An opening about explaining how bees carry pollen between flowers fits the announced talk.

quick_checks: Recognisable unjoined letters/correct cases, useful relative heights/line placement and distinct word spaces.
Spaces separate words so the reader can identify them.
Letter bodies sit relative to the baseline; descending strokes such as g extend below it in the taught form.
Short accurate comfortable practice and feedback; compare more than one comparable attempt for growing ease.
AC9E2LY08.earlier: Add spaces: the big dog. The typed SVG illustrates spacing, not an observed handwritten product.

quick_checks: A phoneme is a speech sound which can distinguish words.
frog has four phonemes: f/r/short-o/g in common Australian pronunciation.
stop without s gives top.
map replacing initial m with t gives tap.
AC9E2LY09.earlier: fish initial f, red initial r, hot middle short-o, bag final g blend as frog.

quick_checks: ai often spells the long a sound as in rain; not a universal rule for every ai word.
k is not separately pronounced in knee; kn spells n here.
sun + set form sunset.
A grapheme is a letter or group of letters used to represent a phoneme in writing.
AC9E2LY10.earlier: rain: r/ai/n map three phonemes; ai represents long a here.

quick_checks: A high-frequency word occurs often in spoken or written language; it may have regular or less predictable spellings.
In said ai represents the short e vowel as in bed; s and d are regular here.
Recognising a meaningful base/affix helps retain spelling and connect meaning despite changes in pronunciation.
Use regular sound mappings to reduce memory load; deliberately learn the unusual spelling rather than memorising only word silhouette.
AC9E2LY11.earlier: Map s, middle vowel short-e, d, and deliberately remember the unusual ai spelling.

quick_checks: A base is the meaningful word/part to which the affix is added in the taught example.
A prefix comes before the base.
-ful often contributes full of/having, e.g. helpful; effect depends on word and conventional use.
playing/player/played/playful are conventional words built with play; accept two suitable ones with meaning.
AC9E2LY12.earlier: helper = help + er and means a person who helps; same meaningful base family.
